stem:
In a physiology laboratory, a 21-year-old student watches a stimulated skeletal muscle fiber contract under the microscope.

Which of the following describes the appearance of its sarcomeres during shortening?

options.label: A
options.text: The I band narrows while the A band stays constant
options.misconception: None; the thin filaments slide over the thick ones, narrowing the I band and H zone.
options.explanation: When a sarcomere contracts, the Z lines move closer together and the I band becomes smaller, while the A band stays the same width because the thick filaments themselves do not change length.

options.label: B
options.text: Both bands narrow to half of their resting width
options.misconception: Shortening is being attributed to the filaments themselves.
options.explanation: The sliding filament model moves filaments past each other rather than shortening them; only the I band (and H zone) narrow, while the A band is unchanged.

options.label: C
options.text: The A band narrows while the I band stays constant
options.misconception: The thick-filament band is being treated as the one that shortens.
options.explanation: The A band reflects the length of the myosin thick filaments, which does not change; it is the I band (thin filament only) that shrinks as the Z lines approach.

options.label: D
options.text: The Z discs move farther apart as the filaments slide
options.misconception: The direction of Z-disc movement is being reversed.
options.explanation: The Z lines move closer together during contraction, pulling the sarcomere's ends toward its center; moving apart would describe stretching.

options.label: E
options.text: The A band widens as extra myosin is laid down
options.misconception: New filament synthesis is being cast as an acute contraction event.
options.explanation: Contraction uses existing filaments and adds nothing new; the A band stays the same width throughout the twitch.

context: Learning objective: read a contracting sarcomere. The sarcomere runs Z-line to Z-line. During contraction the Z lines approach, the I band and H zone shrink, and the A band stays constant because filament length is unchanged — sliding, not shortening, of filaments.
imageCaption: Resting sarcomere: I band narrows on shortening; A band width stays constant.
